claims.text: The as-printed Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has an FCC matrix.
The as-printed alloy has additive-manufacturing-induced melt-pool boundaries.
The as-printed alloy contains residual porosity.
The as-printed alloy exhibits slight chemical segregation.
Elevated-temperature degradation is governed by selective, synergistic oxidation of Cr, Al, and Ti at additive-manufacturing-induced microstructural heterogeneities.
Under oxidizing conditions, a nanocrystalline oxide film enriched in Cr, Al, and Ti forms preferentially along melt-pool boundaries and other microstructural heterogeneities.
The oxide film formed under oxidizing conditions is continuous and adherent.
The Cr-, Al-, and Ti-enriched oxide scale acts as a diffusion barrier.
The diffusion barrier temporarily mitigates further oxidation of the FCC matrix.
The lower oxygen activity in 5% H2 in Ar prevents formation of a continuous protective oxide scale.
Failure to form a continuous protective scale in the reducing atmosphere causes localized chemical depletion.
Reducing-atmosphere exposure produces non-protective or discontinuous oxide patches.
Localized chemical depletion and discontinuous oxide patches weaken interfacial cohesion.
Relative to reducing-atmosphere exposure, oxidizing-atmosphere exposure will produce a more coherent and continuous oxide scale along melt-pool boundaries.
Oxidizing-atmosphere exposure will yield lower bulk-matrix oxidation rates than reducing-atmosphere exposure.
Mechanical integrity will degrade only marginally under oxidizing-atmosphere exposure.
Reducing-atmosphere exposure will cause greater interfacial weakening and earlier microcrack formation than oxidizing-atmosphere exposure.
The as-printed baseline has no significant preformed oxide scale.
